card.name: The verb make before its object
card.fires_on: The verb "make" (made, making) or the word right after it, in older historical prose, where a noun like notes, assessment, examinations or speech is about to follow.

modes.label: make/made itself
modes.description: Forms of "make" used in a light-verb phrase where the object noun comes next.
modes.example: had seen the eggs, but, considering it a common species there, had<< made>> no notes of their number or colour;

modes.label: word after make
modes.description: The determiner or negative right after "made" that opens the object.
modes.example: Sherrard Clemens, of Virginia, made <<a>> strong Union speech in Congress.

card.writes: It nudges the output toward record-like nouns such as copies, transcripts and extracts.
card.plain: It lights up on the verb "make" when a thing like notes, a speech or an assessment is about to be named.
